title: The Festival We Didn't Have to See Together
scene: At an outdoor music festival, two friends discover they want to hear different acts. Instead of forcing a compromise, they agree to enjoy separate performances and meet at a clearly identified fountain afterward.
sceneJa: 野外音楽フェスで、ハナはジャズを聴きたいが、語り手は太鼓の演奏が気になる。無理に同じ演目を選ばず、しばらく別行動をして噴水で合流することに。再会したときには、それぞれ違う話ができた。

chunks.en: Hana wanted to hear the jazz band,
chunks.ja: ハナはジャズバンドを聴きたがっていたが

chunks.en: but I was drawn to the drummers.
chunks.ja: 僕は太鼓の演奏に惹かれていた

chunks.en: "We don't have to stick together the whole time,"
chunks.ja: 「ずっと一緒に回らなくてもいいよ」

chunks.en: "if you'd rather hear the jazz set."
chunks.ja: 「ジャズのほうを聴きたいなら」

chunks.en: "Why don't we split up for a bit
and catch the acts we like?"
chunks.ja: それぞれ好きな演奏を観るのはどう？」

chunks.en: "as long as we pick a meeting spot."
chunks.ja: 「待ち合わせ場所を決めておけばね」
「噴水のところでまた合流しよう
次の演奏が終わったら」

chunks.en: "Just to make sure, the one by the main gate?"
chunks.ja: 「念のため確認だけど、正門のそばの噴水？」

chunks.en: we met up with two different stories to tell.
chunks.ja: それぞれ違う話を持ち寄って再会した

questions.question: Which split keeps the useful phrase 'split up for a bit' together?
options: Why don't we split / up for a / bit and catch the acts we like?
Why don't we / split up for a bit / and catch the acts we like?
Why don't / we split up / for a bit and catch the acts we like?
questions.explanation: 'Split up for a bit' is a natural meaning unit for temporarily going separate ways. It doesn't mean ending the friendship.

questions.question: What does 'We don't have to stick together the whole time' mean here?
options: They can enjoy different acts without staying side by side all day.
They must stop being friends after the festival.
They should stand very close to the stage.
questions.explanation: 'Stick together' can mean staying physically together. The speaker removes the pressure to share every activity.

questions.question: Why does Hana ask 'the one by the main gate?'
options: She wants to change the subject to ticket prices.
She is asking whether the main gate will be closed.
She is confirming the exact meeting place so they can find each other.
questions.explanation: 'Just to make sure' introduces a practical confirmation. They are checking which fountain to use.

speak: Imagine: you and a friend want to watch different performances at a festival. Read: notice that a different preference need not become an argument. Chunk: keep 'don't have to stick together', 'split up for a bit', and 'meet back at' as meaning units. Understand: these express freedom, temporary separation, and a reunion plan. Check: answer the three questions. Speak (30 seconds): explain the two preferences, suggest splitting up, choose a meeting place, and confirm exactly where. Final Read: read all six sentences, pausing after 'for a bit' and stressing 'don't have to' gently rather than forcefully.
review: New: 'don't have to stick together the whole time'（ずっと一緒にいる必要はない）, 'split up for a bit'（少し別行動する）, 'meet back at ...'（〜で再び合流する）. Reuse 'That works for me' (Lesson 107) and 'Just to make sure' (Lesson 110) in a music-festival setting. Compared Lessons 99–112: unlike changing a visit order, splitting a bill, or setting the limits of a ride, this lesson practices giving a friend autonomy while preserving connection. Sources: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/stick-together ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/split-up
